title: The Tomorrow Children
subtitle: A town has to be built from a vanished world

body: The Tomorrow Children is Q-Games' PlayStation 4 social adventure, first made available through its Founder's Pack on 6 September 2016 before a full release in October. Projection clones enter the Void to gather the materials needed to rebuild human communities. The player travels between a town and strange islands, collecting resources and returning them for shared construction. Its visual world resembles a distorted collective future, with work and infrastructure giving the adventure its daily rhythm. Progress is visible in the settlement that the gathered materials allow everyone to extend.

Wood, metal, coal and crystals supply buildings and utilities, while recovered matryoshka dolls contribute to restoring citizens. Buses connect islands to the town, making transport part of the work rather than an invisible transfer between menus. Tools reshape the landscape and reach resources, but enormous Izverg creatures also threaten the settlement. Gathering and defence therefore depend on one another. The player can be useful by bringing back a necessary material or by helping protect what has already been built, with the town providing the common purpose that connects those different activities.

Dylan Cuthbert directed the game, with music by Joel Corelitz. Sony shut down the original service in 2017, ending the first version's short life. Q-Games later acquired the property and released Phoenix Edition in September 2022, introducing changes that included solo play with computer-controlled companions. The revival demonstrates how strongly the design depended on access to its shared world. Its defining idea remains the visible connection between an individual's apparently modest task and the collective settlement: a small delivery matters because it becomes part of something everyone inhabits.
